info.name: Parmana API
info.description:
Generated from openapi/openapi.yaml (API version 1.0.0) by `npm run generate:postman`. Do not edit by hand.

Set `apiKey` in a Postman environment (never commit a key) and, if needed, change `baseUrl`. Requests that need no key use no auth.

item.name: Execution
item.description: Executes a Business Transaction through the complete Execution Trust pipeline

request.description:
A request that runs on a server started with NODE_ENV=test, using the test only capability test:fixture-execute. It was captured live on 2026-09-14 and is approved.

operationId: executeTransaction

Sends one action for a decision and, if approved, performs it. This is the call an agent makes. The
server stores the Business Transaction, evaluates the policy, checks any signed human approval the
policy requires, releases the action to its connector, and returns the signed Execution Trust Record.
It runs synchronously: an approved action that calls an external system took 24 to 32 seconds in
production, so set your client timeout to 120 seconds.

**Before you send:** ask `GET /policies/in-effect?capability=<action>` which policy and version to
declare and which facts to carry.

**Idempotency:** `businessTransactionId` is a UUID you choose and the idempotency key. Sending the
same id again returns `409`; it never runs twice. After a timeout, read
`GET /execution-intents/{businessTransactionId}` before sending anything new.

**What the server sets:** `status`, `createdAt` and `metadata.submittedBy` (from your key). Top level
fields not in the schema are dropped.

**Outcomes:**
1. `200`: approved and released. The body is the signed Trust Record.
2. `403` `POLICY_DENIED`: the policy refused. Final; nothing was released. A Refusal Record is kept at
   `GET /refusal/{businessTransactionId}`.
3. `403` `CAPABILITY_NOT_ALLOWED`, or no code: your key may not invoke this action, or may not act for
   this principal.
4. `503`: refused before release; nothing was executed. See the codes on that response.
5. `502` `EXECUTION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, `executionStatus: EXECUTION_UNKNOWN`: released, then the
   connector call failed, so the outcome is unknown. Do not resend under a new id. Check the target
   system, then close the intent with `POST /execution-intents/{businessTransactionId}/resolve`.
6. `409` `AUTHORIZATION_NO_LONGER_VALID`, `executionStatus: NOT_EXECUTED`: decided, but at release a
   business fact it rested on was past its `validUntil`, or the authority grant had expired or been
   revoked (RFC-0023 phase 4). Nothing was sent. Send a new request.
7. `500` `EXECUTION_RECORD_INCOMPLETE`: released, but the signed record could not be produced. Do not
   resend. An operator rebuilds it with `POST /execution-intents/{businessTransactionId}/finalize`.

The examples named `vendor-payment-flow` show the response shape; their `payments:execute` action no
longer exists. See [Integrate Parmana](/agents/integrate) and the
[Error catalog](/api-reference/error-catalog).

Historical capture (vendor-payment 2.0.0, approved). The payments:execute action no longer exists on a current server. Shown for the response shape only.

query.description: Items per page before filtering to your own transactions. Default 25. Maximum 100.

request.description:
operationId: listTransactions

Lists the Business Transactions your key submitted, as a bare array with no paging metadata. Each
item is the request as stored; for the signed outcome of each, use `GET /trust-records`. A page can hold fewer than `pageSize` items, or none, when other callers'
transactions fall in that window, so keep paging until you have what you need.

Real captured request, currently runnable (test:fixture-execute, the generic NODE_ENV=test-only capability, APPROVED). Prefer this over vendor-payment-flow-transactions-endpoint below, which depends on a connector removed from this repository, see the POST /execute description above for the same caveat.

operationId: createTransaction

The same as `POST /execute` in every way except the success status, `201` instead of `200`. Use
whichever fits your client. Read [Execute a Business Transaction](/api-reference/endpoints/execute-transaction)
for the full behavior, the outcomes and what to do after each.

variable.description: The id you chose when you sent the transaction.

request.description:
operationId: getTransaction

Returns one Business Transaction as it was stored. For the signed outcome, what was decided and
executed, use `GET /trust-records/{businessTransactionId}`.

item.name: Verification
item.description: Deterministic verification of an Execution Trust Record

request.description:
Real captured request

operationId: verifyTransaction

Checks a Trust Record again on the server: recomputes its hash, verifies its signature and checks
that every approved execution is bound to its authorization. All checks run and every failure is
reported. The result is appended to the record as a new Verification. A receipt can only be
generated after a `VERIFIED` result. To verify without trusting this server, use
[Verify independently](/guides/verify-independently).

operationId: getLatestVerification

Returns the most recent Verification appended to a Trust Record by `POST /verify`.

Real captured request

operationId: generateReceipt

Generates a signed Receipt for a Trust Record: a compact proof of what was decided and executed,
to hand to a person or another system. The record must have a `VERIFIED` Verification first; run
`POST /verify`.

operationId: getLatestReceipt

Returns the most recent Receipt for a Trust Record. `POST /execute` generates one for every executed
action.

query.description: Items per page before filtering. Default 25. Maximum 100.
Only include records whose transaction.createdAt is on or after this ISO 8601 timestamp.
Only include records whose transaction.createdAt is on or before this ISO 8601 timestamp.

request.description:
operationId: listTrustRecords

Exports your full, signed Trust Records (transaction, decision, executions, verifications, receipts)
a page at a time, for audit and compliance. Filter by date with `since` and `until`. Paging works as
on `GET /transactions`: a bare array, scoped to your key, and a page can hold fewer than `pageSize`
items.

variable.description: The transaction's id, not the record's `trustRecordId`.

request.description:
operationId: getTrustRecord

Returns the complete signed Execution Trust Record for a transaction: what was asked, what the
policy decided, what was executed and the connector's answer, with signatures. Look it up by the
`businessTransactionId` you chose, not by `trustRecordId`.

item.name: Replay
item.description: Deterministic replay of a recorded Execution Trust Record

request.description:
Real captured request

operationId: replayTransaction

Verifies the stored signature on a Trust Record and returns its hash with the result. It does not
evaluate the policy again and does not execute anything. Nothing is appended to the record; for a
recorded check use `POST /verify`.

item.name: Get the policy a capability's requests must declare right now

query.description: The action, as in `intent.action`, for example `paytm:refund`.

request.description:
operationId: getPolicyInEffect

Tells an agent what a request for a capability must declare and carry right now: the policy name and
version, the policy's description, and its signals (every fact the rules read with its type, the
facts that must equal a value of the intent, and the facts that need a signed human approval with
what that approval must name). Call it before every `POST /execute` instead of hard coding a version:
approving a new version changes the answer with no deploy. The rule conditions are never returned.
Allowed for a key that may invoke the capability, and for human keys.

item.name: Validate that a Policy exists and is readable (vendor-payment)

request.description:
Real captured request

operationId: validatePolicy

Checks that this server can load a policy at a name and version, the same lookup a request uses.
Unlike other routes, every answer, success or failure, has the shape `{ valid, errors }`; only a
`401` uses the usual error body.

item.name: Policy Governance
item.description: Maker-checker proposal, listing, approval, and rejection of policy changes

variable.description: The policy name, for example `customer-refund`. Not `.` or `..`.
The version this proposal changes, for example `1.2.0`. Not `.` or `..`.

request.description:
operationId: proposePolicyChange

Proposes new content for a policy, the maker's step in maker checker governance. Nothing changes
until a different person approves it. `{version}` is the version this proposal changes;
`proposedContent.policyVersion` may be the same (a correction) or new (a new version). The content is
checked as `POST /policies/validate` would, and `proposedContent.policyId` must equal `{name}`. Needs
a human key. See [Policy lifecycle and approvals](/guides/policy-lifecycle-and-approvals).

operationId: listPendingPolicyChanges

Lists policy changes with a diff: the content in effect today (`current`, or `null` for a new version)
next to the proposed content. A checker uses `status=PENDING_APPROVAL` to find what waits for review.
Needs a human key.

operationId: approvePolicyChange

Approves a policy change, the checker's step, and puts it into effect. Checked in order: a human key,
not the person who proposed it, and a step up authorization signed with your step up key for this
change id and action `approve`, valid once. The policy is written and a signed approval record is
kept before the change is marked approved, so a failure never leaves a change approved without
effect. The next request for the bound capability must declare the approved version. See
[Policy governance](/guides/policy-governance-maker-checker).

operationId: rejectPolicyChange

Rejects a policy change. The policy in effect does not change. The same checks as approve, with a
step up authorization for action `reject` and a `rejectionReason`.

item.name: Approvers
item.description: Maker-checker for the keys trusted to sign approvals, without a deploy

request.description:
operationId: listApprovalIssuers

Lists every approver key the server trusts, or once trusted, to sign human approvals for policies
that require one. Keys in the server code come first (`source: code`), then keys added through
approver changes (`source: governed`). Revoked keys stay listed and marked, so every approval ever
accepted can be explained. Needs a human key. See [Manage approvers](/guides/manage-approvers).

operationId: listApprovalIssuerChanges

Lists approver changes, newest first. A checker uses `status=PENDING_APPROVAL` to find what waits for
review. Needs a human key.

item.name: Propose adding or revoking an approver key

body.raw:
{
  "action": "add",
  "approverId": "manager-priya",
  "keyId": "manager-priya-key-1",
  "publicKeyPem": "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\nMCowBQYDK2VwAyEAEDuWHf+bbRY7J/Mr0RVmAKYHH5CDijTWhdnISXWLD6Y=\n-----END PUBLIC KEY-----\n",
  "reason": "Priya approves refunds for the West region from October."
}

request.description:
operationId: proposeApprovalIssuerChange

Proposes trusting a new approver key (`add`, with its Ed25519 public key) or revoking one added this
way (`revoke`). Nothing changes until a different person approves it. Keys in the server code change
only through a pull request. A key id can be added once: to rotate, add a new key id, then revoke the
old one. Needs a human key.

Real captured request

operationId: approveApprovalIssuerChange

Approves an approver change and applies it at once: an added key is trusted from the next approval
checked; a revoked key's approvals are refused from the next request on, including ones it already
signed. Checked in order: a human key, not the proposer, and a step up authorization for this change
id and action `approve`, valid once. The step up authorization is the same one policy changes use,
with the change id in `payload.pendingPolicyChangeId`.

operationId: rejectApprovalIssuerChange

Rejects an approver change. No key changes. The same checks as approve, with a step up authorization
for action `reject` and a `rejectionReason`.

item.name: External Connectors
item.description: Maker-checker for binding a capability to an operator's HTTPS endpoint and its policy, without a deploy (ADR-0013)

request.description:
operationId: listExternalConnectors

Lists every external connector registration, active and revoked: the capability, the HTTPS endpoint
Parmana releases it to, the policy that governs it and the parameters forwarded. Revoked
registrations stay listed, so every release ever made can be explained. Needs a human key. See
[Connect any external system](/guides/connect-any-external-system).

operationId: listExternalConnectorChanges

Lists external connector changes, newest first. A checker uses `status=PENDING_APPROVAL` to find what
waits for review. Needs a human key.

item.name: Propose registering or revoking an external connector (register)

body.raw:
{
  "action": "register",
  "capability": "erp:create-invoice",
  "endpointUrl": "https://erp.example.com/parmana/release",
  "policy": "erp-invoice",
  "allowedParameters": [
    "amount",
    "currency",
    "customerId"
  ],
  "timeoutMs": 10000,
  "reason": "Finance creates invoices in the ERP through Parmana from October."
}

request.description:
Real captured request

operationId: proposeExternalConnectorChange

Proposes connecting your own system to Parmana with no Parmana code change: `register` names a
capability, the HTTPS endpoint to release it to, the policy that governs it, the parameters to
forward and optionally a timeout; `revoke` ends the active registration for a capability. Nothing
changes until a different person approves it. The endpoint must be `https`, name a domain (not an IP
address or localhost), carry no user name, password or fragment, and resolve only to public
addresses; the address is checked again on approval and at every release. Capabilities in a built in
namespace (`paytm`, `hubspot`, `github`, `slack`, `test`) are refused. To move a capability, revoke
it, then register the new endpoint. Needs a human key.

item.name: Propose registering or revoking an external connector (revoke)

request.description:
Real captured request

operationId: proposeExternalConnectorChange

Proposes connecting your own system to Parmana with no Parmana code change: `register` names a
capability, the HTTPS endpoint to release it to, the policy that governs it, the parameters to
forward and optionally a timeout; `revoke` ends the active registration for a capability. Nothing
changes until a different person approves it. The endpoint must be `https`, name a domain (not an IP
address or localhost), carry no user name, password or fragment, and resolve only to public
addresses; the address is checked again on approval and at every release. Capabilities in a built in
namespace (`paytm`, `hubspot`, `github`, `slack`, `test`) are refused. To move a capability, revoke
it, then register the new endpoint. Needs a human key.

Real captured request

operationId: approveExternalConnectorChange

Approves an external connector change and applies it at once: `register` makes the registration
active, `revoke` ends it. For a register, the endpoint's address is checked again first, so a DNS
change since the proposal cannot point it at a private address. Checked in order: a human key, not
the proposer, and a step up authorization for this change id and action `approve`, valid once, with
the change id in `payload.pendingPolicyChangeId`. Requests for the capability are refused until a
version of its policy is approved.

operationId: rejectExternalConnectorChange

Rejects an external connector change. No registration changes. The same checks as approve, with a
step up authorization for action `reject` and a `rejectionReason`.

item.name: Business Signal Sources
item.description: Maker-checker for the business systems Parmana asks for the facts a policy needs, without a deploy (RFC-0023)

request.description:
operationId: listBusinessSignalSources

Lists every business signal source registration, active and revoked: the name a policy's
`signalSources` uses, the HTTPS endpoint Parmana asks, and the Ed25519 key its answers must be
signed with, if one is registered. Revoked registrations stay listed, so every Trusted Signal ever
recorded can be traced to the registration that produced it. Needs a human key. See
[Connect a business system as a signal source](/guides/connect-a-business-signal-source).

operationId: listBusinessSignalSourceChanges

Lists business signal source changes, newest first. A checker uses `status=PENDING_APPROVAL` to
find what waits for review. Needs a human key.

item.name: Propose registering or revoking a business signal source (register)

body.raw:
{
  "action": "register",
  "name": "erp",
  "endpointUrl": "https://orders.example.com/parmana/signals",
  "timeoutMs": 5000,
  "publicKeyPem": "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\nMCowBQYDK2VwAyEAsgWd/PtRf9OsENif9bgJegghUpmEOOZN5NROxc3zpPc=\n-----END PUBLIC KEY-----\n",
  "keyId": "erp-2026-10",
  "reason": "Release goods only against invoices the ERP says are paid."
}

request.description:
Real captured request

operationId: proposeBusinessSignalSourceChange

Proposes connecting a business system, any system that owns facts a policy needs (an ERP, an
order system, a CRM, a ledger), so Parmana can ask it instead of trusting the agent's claim.
`register` names the source, the HTTPS endpoint Parmana asks, optionally a timeout, and optionally
the Ed25519 public key the source signs its answers with; `revoke` ends the active registration
for a name. Nothing changes until a different person approves it. The endpoint must be `https`,
name a domain (not an IP address or localhost), carry no user name, password or fragment, and
resolve only to public addresses; the address is checked again on approval and at every query.
To move a source, revoke it, then register the new endpoint. Needs a human key.

item.name: Propose registering or revoking a business signal source (revoke)

request.description:
Real captured request

operationId: proposeBusinessSignalSourceChange

Proposes connecting a business system, any system that owns facts a policy needs (an ERP, an
order system, a CRM, a ledger), so Parmana can ask it instead of trusting the agent's claim.
`register` names the source, the HTTPS endpoint Parmana asks, optionally a timeout, and optionally
the Ed25519 public key the source signs its answers with; `revoke` ends the active registration
for a name. Nothing changes until a different person approves it. The endpoint must be `https`,
name a domain (not an IP address or localhost), carry no user name, password or fragment, and
resolve only to public addresses; the address is checked again on approval and at every query.
To move a source, revoke it, then register the new endpoint. Needs a human key.

item.name: Approve a business signal source change

request.description:
Real captured request

operationId: approveBusinessSignalSourceChange

Approves a business signal source change and applies it at once: `register` makes the
registration active, so policies that name it can be evaluated; `revoke` ends it, so they are
refused as `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`. For a register, the endpoint's address is checked again first.
Checked in order: a human key, not the proposer, and a step up authorization for this change id
and action `approve`, valid once, with the change id in `payload.pendingPolicyChangeId`.

item.name: Reject a business signal source change

request.description:
operationId: rejectBusinessSignalSourceChange

Rejects a business signal source change. No registration changes. The same checks as approve,
with a step up authorization for action `reject` and a `rejectionReason`.

item.name: Authority Grants
item.description: Maker-checker for which agent may have which action decided, within which limits, until when (RFC-0023)

request.description:
operationId: listAuthorityGrants

Lists every authority grant, active and revoked: which caller may have which capability decided,
within which limits, from when until when. A grant matters only under a policy with
`requireAuthorityGrant`. Revoked grants stay listed, so every decision that rested on one can be
explained. Needs a human key. See [Grant an agent authority](/guides/grant-an-agent-authority).

operationId: listAuthorityGrantChanges

Lists authority grant changes, newest first. A checker uses `status=PENDING_APPROVAL` to find what
waits for review. Needs a human key.

item.name: Propose granting or revoking an agent's authority (grant)

request.description:
Real captured request

operationId: proposeAuthorityGrantChange

Proposes per-agent authority (RFC-0023 phase 3): `grant` says the API key with `callerId` may have
requests for `capability` decided, within `limits` on the request, until `validUntil` (at most 366
days); `revoke` ends the active grant. Nothing changes until a different person approves it. You
may not propose authority for your own key. Under a policy with `requireAuthorityGrant`, a request
from a key with no grant in force, or outside its limits, is refused as `NOT_AUTHORIZED`, and one
after `validUntil` as `AUTHORITY_EXPIRED`. To change a grant, revoke it, then grant again. Needs a
human key.

item.name: Propose granting or revoking an agent's authority (revoke)

request.description:
Real captured request

operationId: proposeAuthorityGrantChange

Proposes per-agent authority (RFC-0023 phase 3): `grant` says the API key with `callerId` may have
requests for `capability` decided, within `limits` on the request, until `validUntil` (at most 366
days); `revoke` ends the active grant. Nothing changes until a different person approves it. You
may not propose authority for your own key. Under a policy with `requireAuthorityGrant`, a request
from a key with no grant in force, or outside its limits, is refused as `NOT_AUTHORIZED`, and one
after `validUntil` as `AUTHORITY_EXPIRED`. To change a grant, revoke it, then grant again. Needs a
human key.

Real captured request

operationId: approveAuthorityGrantChange

Approves an authority grant change and applies it at once: `grant` makes the grant active,
starting now unless it names a later `validFrom`; `revoke` ends it, so the caller's next request
under a policy with `requireAuthorityGrant` is refused. A grant whose `validUntil` has passed is
refused. Checked in order: a human key, not the proposer, not the grantee, and a step up
authorization for this change id and action `approve`, valid once, with the change id in
`payload.pendingPolicyChangeId`.

operationId: rejectAuthorityGrantChange

Rejects an authority grant change. No grant changes. The same checks as approve, with a step up
authorization for action `reject` and a `rejectionReason`.

item.name: Sandbox
item.description: Routes that exist only on the public sandbox (ADR-0014), for trying Parmana from a browser

request.description:
operationId: createSandboxApproval

**Sandbox only.** Returns an approval signed by the sandbox's demo approver, so you can try an approved
request from a browser. In production a person signs every approval with their own key on their own
machine; this route does not exist there.

It signs only for `sandbox:receipt`, for the one `resourceId` you name (the target of the request you will
send), valid 5 minutes. Put it in your request's `signals.approvalArtifact`. `POST /execute` checks it like
any other approval: a trusted approver key, the signature, the capability, the resource and the expiry, and
it accepts it once. Needs the published demo key.

Live at `https://parmana-sandbox.vercel.app`. The request that uses it carries
`signals: { "note": "<the same text as parameters.note>", "receiptApproved": true, "approvalArtifact": <this response> }`,
with `target` equal to the `resourceId` you named here. The [Playground](/playground) walks through every step.

item.name: Refusal Records
item.description: Durable, signed evidence that a policy decision rejected a transaction (RFC-0021)

request.description:
operationId: verifyRefusalRecord

Checks a Refusal Record's signature. Send the record itself; the server reads no storage and needs no
key, so anyone holding a refusal can prove Parmana issued it and that it was not changed. Fetch the
record with `GET /refusal/{businessTransactionId}`.

item.name: Get a Refusal Record by transaction ID

variable.description: The id of the refused transaction.

request.description:
operationId: getRefusalRecord

Returns the signed Refusal Record kept when a policy refused a transaction: the decision, the rule
that refused, the facts it saw and the signature. Use it to show a person why an action was refused,
or pass it to `POST /refusal/verify`, which anyone can call.

  }
}

request.description:
operationId: verifyExecutionIntent

Checks an Execution Intent's hash and signature. Send the intent itself; the server reads no storage
and needs no key. A valid intent proves Parmana signed it before release and that it was not changed.
It does not prove the action ran: an intent is written before release. For the outcome, read the
Trust Record for the same transaction.

item.name: List Execution Intents that never reached a signed Trust Record

query.description: How many intents to return. Default 50, at most 200.

request.description:
operationId: listUnfinalizedExecutionIntents

The operator's work queue: Execution Intents that never reached a signed Trust Record and were not
closed by hand, oldest first. Each one is an action that may have been performed without a record.
For an intent in state `RELEASED`, rebuild the record with `POST .../finalize`. For `PREPARED` or
`ERRORED`, check the target system, then close it with `POST .../resolve`. Needs a human key, because
the list spans every caller. See [Execution Intents](/concepts/execution-intents).

item.name: Get an Execution Intent and its status

request.description:
operationId: getExecutionIntent

Returns the signed Execution Intent for a transaction and where it got to. Read it after a timeout or
a `5xx` before sending anything new. The `status.state` is one of:

* `PREPARED`: signed and stored; the action may or may not have been released.
* `RELEASED`: released and its result saved.
* `FINALIZED`: a signed Trust Record exists.
* `ERRORED`: the release failed; the action may still have run.
* `RESOLVED`: a person checked the target system and closed it (`resolution`, `resolutionNote`,
  `resolvedBy`, `resolvedAt`; an unsigned statement).

item.name: Rebuild the signed Trust Record for a released action

request.description:
operationId: finalizeExecutionIntent

Rebuilds the signed Trust Record for an action that was released but whose record was never
produced, the repair for a `500` `EXECUTION_RECORD_INCOMPLETE`. It never calls the connector: it uses
the result saved right after release, then verifies the record and generates its receipt. Safe to
repeat: "if a record exists it returns it as `ALREADY_FINALIZED` and builds nothing. Needs a human key."

item.name: Close an intent you reconciled by hand

request.description:
operationId: resolveExecutionIntent

Closes an intent in state `PREPARED` or `ERRORED` after a person checked the target system, the
repair for a `502` `EXECUTION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`. Record what you found, `NOT_EXECUTED` or `EXECUTED`,
with a note. The intent becomes `RESOLVED` and leaves the unfinalized list. It never calls the
connector. Safe to repeat: a second call returns `ALREADY_RESOLVED` with the first answer.
**The resolution is an attributed, timestamped statement in the intent's unsigned status. It is not
tamper evident and it is not a Trust Record.** Needs a human key.

item.name: Audit
item.description: Signed caller-authentication audit events, independently third-party-verifiable

item.name: Verify a signed caller-authentication audit event

request.description:
operationId: verifyAuditEvent

Checks the signature of a caller authentication audit event, the record the server keeps of every
authentication, denial and governance action. Send the event and its signature; the server reads no
storage and needs no key. Only production audit trails sign events. See
[Caller audit trail](/concepts/caller-audit-trail).

operationId: getRoot

Returns the service name and `UP`. Use it to check that your key is accepted: unlike `GET /health`,
this route requires a key.

operationId: getHealth

Liveness probe. Always returns `UP` while the process is serving requests; it checks no dependency.
Needs no key. For a check that includes storage, use `GET /ready`.

operationId: getReady

Readiness probe. When storage is Postgres, it runs `SELECT 1` so an orchestrator can tell a process
that is up but cannot reach its database from one that can serve traffic. With in memory storage
there is nothing to check and it always returns `READY`. Needs no key.

operationId: getOpenApiSpec

This API's complete OpenAPI 3.1 document as YAML, self contained with no external references. Needs
no key, so a client can discover the API before it has one. Load it into a code generator, Postman or
an agent. `GET /openapi.json` serves the same document as JSON.

item.name: Get the OpenAPI spec, as JSON

request.description:
operationId: getOpenApiSpecJson

The same document as `GET /openapi.yaml`, as JSON, for tools and agents that expect a spec at a
`.json` path. Needs no key.

operationId: getApiManifest

One index for agents and tools: where the OpenAPI document and the rendered references are, how to
authenticate, and both official SDKs with their package name, registry and current version. Read it
first when an agent sets itself up. Go and Java are `null` because no SDK exists for them; call the
REST API directly. Needs no key.

operationId: getVersion

Returns `name`, `version` and `api`. These are literals in the server code, not a build number, so do
not use them to detect a deploy. The SDKs carry their own versions; see
`GET /api-manifest.json`.

item.name: Fetch a public signing key for independent, offline verification

variable.description: The `keyId` named in the signature you want to verify, for example `default`.

request.description:
operationId: getKey

Returns the public half of a signing key, so anyone can verify a Parmana signature without a Parmana
account: "an auditor, a regulator, or an endpoint receiving a release. Every signed artifact names its"
`keyId`; pass it here. Keys that were rotated out stay available as long as the server keeps them, so
old records remain verifiable. Use the `pem` field with the SDK verifiers (`verifyParmanaRelease`,
`verify_parmana_release`) or the offline verifier. Needs no key.

item.name: List every public signing key this deployment can currently produce

request.description:
operationId: getJwks

Lists every public signing key this deployment can serve, the enumeration form of `GET /keys/{keyId}`.
With local key files that is every key in the key directory. Under AWS KMS it is the keys this
deployment signs with: `default` and the current `PARMANA_VERIFICATION_KEY_ID`. A record signed
under an older key id is still served by `GET /keys/{keyId}`. Fetch and cache it when you verify
many artifacts. Not a strict RFC 7517 JWK Set: use the `pem` of each entry; an entry may have no
`jwk` field. Needs no key.

item.name: Get the authenticated caller's identity and resolved scope

request.description:
operationId: getCallerMe

Returns who your key is and exactly what it may do: the caller id, the principals it may act for, the
capabilities it may invoke and whether that includes every capability (`*`), after defaults are
applied. Call it
first when you set up an agent, and show it in a security review. An unset `allowedPrincipalIds`
means the caller's own id; an unset `allowedCapabilities` means none. Never returns key material, and
never another caller's record.

operationId: getHandbookPdf

Downloads the Parmana Handbook as a PDF. Needs no key.

item.name: Capture an email address, then redirect straight to the handbook PDF

request.description:
operationId: getHandbookDownloadLead

Records an email address, then redirects to the handbook PDF. Backs the download form on the docs
site, which submits with a plain GET. The address is stored, not verified. Needs no key. For a JSON
answer use `POST /handbook/download-leads`.

item.name: Capture an email address before unlocking the handbook PDF download

request.description:
operationId: createHandbookDownloadLead

Records an email address and returns the handbook download link as JSON. The address is stored, not
verified. Needs no key.
